fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**
Large cut stone slabs, laid dry, cracked. Grey-brown, dressed flat, no mortar you'd feel.
fields.Q1_WHY: In the lighting-normalized pass the top band (x 60–380, y 150–230) resolves into portrait-format slabs roughly 30×70 px with hard 2 px black joints, and the right band (x 620–750, y 300–760) resolves into horizontal running-bond courses with 4 px black joints — measurably harder joints than the floor's (hard-dark pixel fraction per column jumps from ~0.05 on floor columns to 0.15–0.42 from x≈620 rightward). But I have to state the caveat plainly: **I only know this because I gamma-boosted it.** Raw luminance of the left band (x 0–54, y 300–700) is mean 9.1 / std 4.3 out of 255. The right band (x 695–749) is mean 6.9 / std 2.3. The bottom band (y 776–830) is mean 10.4 / std 3.1. At those numbers there is no material on screen.
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR FLAT PATTERN?**
**Flat pattern.** Nothing in the image gives the walls thickness. There is no cap face distinguished from a side face, no cast shadow at the wall base, no occlusion at the corners, no lip anywhere. What separates room from not-room is a 2 px black hairline — at y=230–232 across the top, x=55–56 on the left, y=770–773 along the bottom — and those hairlines are the same width and the same value as ordinary joints inside the floor field. At y=490 the floor→wall boundary on the right (x≈620, 44→22) is indistinguishable from the joints at x=596, 640, 660, 684 on the same row.

Worse for the read: at y 300–700 the left wall averages luminance **9.1** and the floor strip immediately inside it (x 60–114) averages **9.2**. Identical brightness. The only thing separating standing stone from walkable ground at equal radius is texture variance (std 4.3 vs 12.2), which is not something an eye resolves at these levels.
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**
Cleanest transition is the top edge at **x=300, y=228→234**: 18 → **3** → 10. Six pixels, of which the actual event is a 2-pixel black line, and the material either side of it is the same value (16–18 above, 10–17 below). That is the whole transition. On the left (x=55–56, y=490 row) it is the same 2 px line, and the values across it run 5→2→7 — a change of five levels out of 255. On the **right side I cannot tell you where the ground stops from the image as shown.** The x=490 row from x=620 to x=749 is a monotone decay 54→5 interrupted by five equal-looking joints; nothing marks one of them as the boundary. That is a real answer, not a dodge.
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**
**NOTHING.** No ties, no pins, no rope, no timber, no strapping, no bracing, no shoring. One candidate: at **(133–146, 190–225)** in the top band there is a vertical bar crossed by three horizontal bars — reads as a driven pin with washers, or a bracket. It is 14×35 px, it spans no joint, it bridges no crack, and it is invisible at raw luminance (that region reads 12–20). It is a decal on a face, not a fastening. There is also a solid black rectangle with drip pixels at **(206–236, 172–181)** — a hole or a hanging plate, again attached to nothing. Cut either and the room stands exactly as it does now.
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR REPEATED?**
**Repeated**, and I can prove it rather than assert it.

Two 28×54 px crack sprites in the bottom band — at **x 143–171** and **x 271–299**, both at y 776–830 — are **pixel-for-pixel identical**, 264 set pixels each, at zero vertical offset, exactly 128 px apart. Not similar. Identical.

An exact-hash scan over 32×32 blocks finds the same near-black motif (128 set pixels) at **(56,202), (272,202), (476,202), (494,202)** — four copies at the *same* y within the top band, one pair only 18 px apart. Same test: **(292,230) ≡ (488,230)**; **(94,770) ≡ (218,770)**.

Autocorrelation confirms the character. Along the bottom band, correlation stays at **0.60–0.68 for every shift from 16 to 160 px**, with a peak at d=64 and its harmonic at d=128. The floor, same test, decays from 0.24 to 0.02 by d=128. The floor varies with position; the wall band is statistically the same strip everywhere along its length.

One more measurement, and it is the one I'd want on the record: I tested whether each band carries odd-row information. Fraction of adjacent row-pairs that are byte-identical — **left wall 1.00**, bottom wall 0.97, top wall 0.96, right wall 0.93; **mid floor 0.33**. The left wall has *zero* odd-row detail. The standing structure is authored at half the floor's resolution and nearest-neighbour doubled. Confirmed independently by the crack glyph itself, which is drawn entirely in 2×2 blocks.
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED?**
**YES.** Plenty of commercial top-down games ship walls that are functionally black at play brightness.

Merely competent, or genuinely good? **Merely competent, and only on the strength of work that isn't the wall.** The floor and the light falloff are good. The standing structure is half-resolution art, stamped with duplicated decals, rendered at 3–13% luminance, bounded by a hairline. Judged as the subject, it is not good.
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES AT 1:1?**
**Blank.** All four bands. Not "subtle" — blank.

Legible at 1:1: the 2 px black boundary hairline (top only, and only because it hits luminance 3 against a 10–18 field); the black crack squiggles in the top band where they cross the brighter base course; the fact that something is darker up there than down here. That is the complete list.

Only on magnification + gamma: the slab coursing, the joint pattern, the running bond on the right, the bracket at (133,190), the blob-and-drips at (206,172), the moisture blooms in the left band around y 520–560, the tick-marked base course at y 233–262.

Does it change with distance? Yes, and not enough to rescue it. The best-lit wall in the frame is the right band at its nearest point (x 620–660, y 460–520): mean **33**, max **72** — you can just make out coursing there. The base course directly north of the figure (x 380–440, y 235–262) is mean **24**, max **38**. Everything beyond that radius — the whole left band, the whole bottom band, the outer two-thirds of the top band — is under 12 mean. Compare the floor at the figure: mean **123**, std **30**. The wall never reaches a quarter of what the floor gets at its own best point.
fields.Q7_WHY: Checked at 1:1 — (280,200)–(540,290) the base course north of the figure; (640,420)–(750,560) the right band at its brightest; (200,730)–(520,830) the bottom band; (20,420)–(140,560) the left band at the figure's row. Had to magnify (4–6×) and gamma-lift (γ≈0.25–0.28) — (60,150)–(380,300) to find the coursing and the bracket; (540,260)–(750,560) to find the running bond; (60,770)–(450,832) to find the bottom band's structure; (0,240)–(120,780) to find the left band's stains.
fields.Q8:
ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**
Yes, three things.

1. **The crack squiggle.** A near-vertical 1–2 px zigzag, always the same gesture, always full-height in its band. In the bottom band alone it appears at x ≈ 17, 84, 157, 211, 285, 346, 426, 460, 520, 581, 669, 745 — twelve, one roughly every 62 px, which is two grid cells. Same rhythm in the top band. Two of them (157, 285) are the identical sprite.
2. **The same motif at the same height in every bay.** (56,202), (272,202), (476,202), (494,202) — same y, four times.
3. **Near-black pixel density.** Top band 0.131, bottom 0.093, left 0.173 — against floor **0.008**. Every band is ~12–20× more shot through with black hairlines than the floor is. Read as a whole, the walls are a black-scribble field.
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**
Two different answers, and neither is good.

Beyond the left/right/bottom bands: **more of exactly the same stuff.** The bands run to the frame edge with no terminus, no far side, no change of any kind. Nothing says the room is inside anything.

At the top, there are two **hard-edged black quads** — top-left roughly x 0–247, y 22–133; top-right x 563–750, same rows. The left one measured: mean 1.11, **std 0.00, one unique value across 100×220 px**, edges perfectly axis-aligned. That is a fog-of-war primitive, not darkness. And its bottom edge at y=133 slices straight through the middle of the top wall band, cutting masonry mid-slab with no regard for the wall's own geometry. It doesn't read as unknown space; it reads as a rectangle laid on top of the picture.
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH WITHOUT WALKING INTO IT?**
Found it: **x 375–438** (63 px, two cells), running north from y≈232 to the top of the frame. The y=231 dark line is continuous from x=55 to x=374, breaks — values jump to 9, 13, 17, 21, 22 — and resumes at x=439 through 749.

**I read it as a passage, but only just, and not for the reason it should be.** What sells it is the *absence* of the boundary line plus a luminance gradient: the vertical profile at x=405 rises monotonically from y=200 to y=300 with no seam, whereas at x=300 it hits 3 at y=230. So the cue is negative — a gap in a line — not positive.

Two things actively work against it. The corridor is jambed by two 2 px black lines at x≈377 and x≈439 with **no reveal, no jamb thickness, no threshold, no occlusion shadow** — nothing that says you're passing between two masses. And the fill inside the corridor is a smooth mottled grey-blue that **does not match the room floor's flagstones**, so it doesn't read as floor continuing through an opening; it reads as a differently-textured column. A notch and a passage are being distinguished here by the absence of a two-pixel line. That is too thin.
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**
It is cracked, damp, and **completely untouched**. Cracks in every band at 12–20× the floor's density; moisture blooms in the left band around y 520–560; something dark has run down from (206,172) leaving drip pixels. That's decay.

What is absent is the more telling read: **there is not one repair anywhere on this structure.** No rope, no driven pin bridging a crack, no hide, no salvaged timber, no patch, no shoring, no course reset. The one bracket-like object at (133,190) spans nothing. Every crack runs its full length unremedied, and the same crack runs unremedied twice at x=157 and x=285. The fiction says a company has held and repaired this line for four hundred years and is extremely good at it. What is on screen is a place nobody has entered.
fields.CULL: Walls are half-resolution art with duplicated decals, invisible at play brightness — the subject isn't rendered.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Lift the standing bands off the floor in value at equal radius — the left wall currently reads 9.1 against a 9.2 floor. Give the wall its own falloff floor (~2× the ground's minimum) so the room stays bounded when the light is 250 px away.
- Give the walls thickness: a distinct cap face vs. side face, and a 3–4 px contact shadow where every band meets the ground. Right now the entire boundary is a 2 px hairline identical to a floor joint.
- Kill the duplicate decals. `(143,776)≡(271,776)` is pixel-exact; `(56,202)`, `(272,202)`, `(476,202)`, `(494,202)` are the same 32×32 motif at the same height. Mirror, offset vertically, or author more variants — the current bottom band autocorrelates at 0.6+ across every shift out to 160 px.
- Author the walls at the floor's resolution. Left band is 1.00 row-pair-identical (zero odd-row information) against 0.33 for mid floor.
- Make the north opening at x 375–438 read positively: give it jamb depth, an occlusion shadow at the threshold, and floor texture continuing through it instead of the mismatched grey fill it has now.

The pattern behind all five: the authored detail exists — coursing, bond, stains, a bracket — and the lighting deletes it before the player can see any of it. This is a render-and-value problem sitting on top of an art problem, and fixing the art without fixing the value curve will change nothing on screen.

*Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)*
